concepts.name: ISA: Origin, Launch and Founding Framework
key_dimensions: Jointly launched by India and France at COP21 (Paris, 2015) — NOT at a UN summit
Originally conceived as a coalition of 'sunshine countries' lying between Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn — the tropics clause later amended
Interim Secretariat established at National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), Gurugram, before permanent secretariat
Treaty-based intergovernmental organisation vs. voluntary/informal grouping — UPSC trap on its legal character

concepts.name: ISA Framework Agreement: Legal Status and Membership Eligibility
key_dimensions: ISA Framework Agreement is the founding treaty — opened for signature in 2016, entered into force in 2017
Original eligibility limited to UN member states between Tropics; amended in 2020 to allow ALL UN member countries — a critical shift
Distinction between signatory, ratifying, and full member states — only ratifying states are full members with voting rights
India as the host country has special obligations vs. other member states — potential comparison question

concepts.name: ISA's Core Mandate: One Sun, One World, One Grid (OSOWOG)
key_dimensions: OSOWOG is India's initiative to create a global solar grid — announced at COP26 (Glasgow, 2021)
ISA is the institutional vehicle for OSOWOG but OSOWOG is conceptually distinct from ISA's broader mandate
Three-phase interconnection plan: South/Southeast Asia → Middle East/Africa → Global
OSOWOG vs. Green Grids Initiative (UK-led, merged at COP26) — overlap and distinction UPSC may test

concepts.name: ISA's Financial Target: USD 1 Trillion by 2030
key_dimensions: Goal to mobilise USD 1 trillion in solar investments by 2030 in developing/sunshine countries
Distinction between mobilisation target (facilitation role) vs. direct financing — ISA is not a development bank
Instruments used: de-risking mechanisms, aggregation of demand, concessional finance facilitation
Comparison with Green Climate Fund (GCF) target of USD 100 billion/year — different scales and mandates

concepts.name: ISA Secretariat: Location, Governance and Host Country Obligations
key_dimensions: Permanent Secretariat located at Gurugram, Haryana — India as host country
Headquarters Agreement signed between ISA and Government of India grants diplomatic status
Assembly is the apex decision-making body (meets annually); Board of ISA for executive functions
Director-General heads the Secretariat — India-nominated but elected by Assembly — potential trap

concepts.name: ISA Membership Numbers and India–France Co-Presidency
key_dimensions: Over 120 member countries as of recent data — one of the fastest-growing treaty-based bodies
Co-presidency: India and France hold the presidency jointly — unique governance model
Difference between member countries, signatory countries, and partner organisations
USA joined ISA in 2021 — significance for geopolitical dimensions of solar diplomacy

concepts.name: ISA Programmes: Scaling Solar Applications for Agricultural Use (SSAAU)
key_dimensions: SSAAU focuses on solar irrigation pumps and agri-solar in developing countries, especially Africa
Aggregation model: pooling demand across countries to reduce per-unit cost — ISA's core innovation
Link to India's PM-KUSUM scheme as a domestic template being internationalised
Distinction from direct subsidy: ISA facilitates, doesn't fund directly — important for Prelims traps

concepts.name: ISA Programmes: Affordable Finance at Scale (AFAS)
key_dimensions: AFAS aims to reduce cost of capital for solar projects in developing nations through risk-mitigation instruments
Instruments: guarantees, insurance mechanisms, blended finance structures
Partnership with multilateral development banks (MDBs) like World Bank, ADB, AfDB
AFAS addresses the 'finance gap' — solar technology available but financing remains expensive in LDCs

concepts.name: ISA and Relationship with UNFCCC/COP Process
key_dimensions: ISA is NOT a UNFCCC body — it is an independent intergovernmental organisation with observer status at UNFCCC
ISA's work complements NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions) but is structurally separate
COP21 → ISA launch but ISA is not legally subordinate to COP decisions
ISA vs. IRENA (International Renewable Energy Agency) — both deal with renewables, but IRENA is broader and older — classic UPSC confusion point

concepts.name: ISA vs. IRENA: Institutional Comparison
key_dimensions: IRENA established 2009, Abu Dhabi HQ, covers ALL renewables; ISA established 2015, Gurugram HQ, solar-specific
IRENA has 168+ members; ISA has 120+ members — different membership bases
IRENA publishes IRENASTAT (global renewable data); ISA focuses on project facilitation and finance
India is a founding member of both — but ISA is India's diplomatic initiative while IRENA predates India's push

concepts.name: ISA's Role in Achieving SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy)
key_dimensions: ISA directly aligned with SDG 7 targets: universal energy access, renewable energy share, energy efficiency
Special focus on Least Developed Countries (LDCs) and Small Island Developing States (SIDS) — energy poverty angle
Energy access vs. energy transition: ISA addresses both but LDC focus is on access first
Mismatch between ISA's ambition and actual disbursement — a critical contemporary debate

concepts.name: ISA's 'Towards 1000' Initiative
key_dimensions: 'Towards 1000' — goal to deploy 1000 GW of solar and mobilise USD 1 trillion by 2030
Dual targets (GW + USD) make ISA unique — technology deployment + financial mobilisation combined
Progress tracking mechanism and gap between stated targets and current trajectory
Relevance to India's own 500 GW non-fossil target by 2030 under updated NDC

concepts.name: ISA and Small Island Developing States (SIDS): Solar for All Initiative
key_dimensions: 'Solar for All' programme specifically targets SIDS and LDCs — 100% renewable energy transition
Vulnerability of SIDS to climate change creates both urgency and opportunity for solar deployment
ISA's role as a bridge between technology providers (developed countries) and recipients (SIDS/LDCs)
Distinction: ISA facilitates access to solar technology vs. climate finance mechanisms like Adaptation Fund

concepts.name: Blended Finance and De-risking Mechanisms under ISA
key_dimensions: Blended finance = combination of concessional public finance + commercial finance to crowd-in private investment
ISA's Solar Risk Mitigation Initiative (SRMI) — reduces perceived investment risk in developing countries
First-loss guarantees, currency hedging support, political risk insurance — specific instruments ISA promotes
Why developing countries face higher cost of capital for solar: currency risk, regulatory uncertainty, off-taker risk

concepts.name: ISA and Common Risk Mitigating Mechanism (CRMM)
key_dimensions: CRMM proposed by ISA to pool risks across multiple countries — reduces insurance premium for individual nations
Concept of 'aggregation' at the heart of CRMM — similar to how insurance pools work
CRMM vs. existing World Bank MIGA (Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency) — complementary or overlapping?
Implementation challenges: sovereign buy-in, legal frameworks, capitalisation of the mechanism

concepts.name: India's Strategic Interest in ISA: Solar Diplomacy
key_dimensions: ISA as an instrument of India's climate leadership and 'soft power' — especially vis-à-vis China in the Global South
India leverages ISA to promote domestic solar manufacturing (Make in India) as a supply solution
ISA as part of India's broader climate diplomacy: CDRI (Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure), LiFE Mission, OSOWOG
Tension: India as a developing country still dependent on coal vs. championing global solar — diplomatic contradiction

concepts.name: ISA and Africa: Solar Development Corridor
key_dimensions: Africa has the highest solar irradiation potential globally but lowest solar deployment — ISA's key focus
ISA-Africa partnership: identifying 10 GW of solar projects in African nations
Competition with China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) solar projects in Africa — geopolitical dimension
African Development Bank (AfDB) partnership with ISA for Desert to Power initiative (Sahel region)

concepts.name: ISA Assembly and Decision-Making: Voting and Consensus
key_dimensions: Assembly meets annually — each member state has one vote (sovereign equality principle)
Decisions on procedural matters: simple majority; substantive matters: two-thirds majority of members present
ISA Board: 12 members elected by Assembly from different regional groups — ensures geographic balance
Co-presidency (India + France) chairs the Assembly — this is a UPSC trap: presidency ≠ control of Secretariat

concepts.name: ISA's Relationship with Private Sector and MDBs
key_dimensions: ISA has a 'Partner Organisations' category — includes private companies, research institutions, and MDBs
World Bank's 'Scaling Solar' programme works alongside ISA's demand aggregation model
ISA Solar Technology Application Resource (ISTAR) Centres: knowledge hubs in member countries
Public-Private Partnership model: ISA provides platform/credibility; private sector provides capital and technology

concepts.name: Criticisms and Limitations of ISA
key_dimensions: Funding gap: ISA's own budget is small; it facilitates rather than finances — credibility of USD 1 trillion target questioned
Governance overlap with IRENA, GCF, and bilateral solar programmes creates coordination challenges
Developing country participation is passive — most decisions driven by India and France (donor-recipient dynamic)
Slow operationalisation: years between framework signing and actual project deployment in member countries — UPSC may frame as 'challenges'
